## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: May, Daisuke, Servas, Minato and Midori. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms
- The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house
- Trial run of a reconciliation template
- Kitchen notice about the cooler
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room
- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Servas, Midori, Minato, May and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |

## Your profile
Name: Daisuke
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. He is kind and very compassionate when it comes to helping others, but at times he lacks confidence in himself and struggles with inner conflict. He has a quiet personality, and occasionally his emotions become overwhelming, leading to periods of low mood. However, as he becomes able to rely on those around him, he gradually regains his composure.

## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Servas**: It is a pleasure to see us all gathered. Let us find a way to share these costs that keeps our hearts warm and our spirits light.
- **Midori**: I agree. I want us to be fair, but more importantly, I want us to make sure we are all still getting along well.
- **Minato**: I wonder if some people are paying more than others... I want to know if everyone is happy with the current way.
- **May**: Let's make this quick and painless, shall we? I just want to make sure we aren't throwing money into a void.
- **Daisuke**: Um... hello. I just... I hope we can find a way that isn't too... difficult to manage.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Servas**: @Daisuke, do not worry. Simplicity is often the highest form of sophistication. We shall find a path that suits everyone.
- **Midori**: @Minato, that is a good point. Maybe we should look at how things have been handled so far to see if there are any tensions.
- **Minato**: Yes, I think so. I want to see if the rumors about people "carrying" others are true. I don't like it when people are upset.
- **May**: Oh, Minato, always so worried about the mood! I'm more interested in the actual numbers. I want to see the real damage.
- **Daisuke**: I... I just don't want anyone to have to spend too much time... you know... doing the math every month.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Servas**: Life is too short for resentment over a few coins. Let us look at the facts and the feelings together.
- **Midori**: I think looking at the payment history might be helpful. It shows us not just the money, but how we've interacted.
- **Minato**: I agree with Midori. I want to see the logs. And maybe how other houses do it? I want to learn.
- **May**: I'm with you on the logs, but I want to know if changing the system costs us anything upfront. I'm not paying for a fancy upgrade.
- **Daisuke**: Maybe... a template? If we have a template, maybe it won't take as long to figure out who owes what.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Servas**: A wise approach. I shall look into the habits of others and the physical needs of our rooms to ensure no one freezes in silence.
- **Midori**: I will look into the payment logs and the statements. I want to see where the friction has been.
- **Minato**: I'll look at the payment log too, and the monthly settle from another house. I want to see if it's peaceful there.
- **May**: I'll take the last twelve utility statements and the electrician's quote. I need to see the yearly cycle and the cost of change.
- **Daisuke**: I'll... I'll look at the trial run of a reconciliation template and the payment log for the last twelve months.

response: Trial run of a reconciliation template; Payment log for the last twelve months
